Answer: B
Reason: The first image (3-year-old) displays multiple subpleural cystic spaces and linear interstitial thickening predominantly in the upper lobes, characteristic of early-stage pulmonary involvement in Down syndrome. The second image (12-year-old) shows clear lung fields with no visible cysts or significant interstitial markings, indicating a normal chest X-ray appearance for that age in this context.
